items.title: Published cut-offs have never been validated
items.whyItMatters: Cut-offs derived in the same data overstate accuracy (claims c1, c2).
items.opportunity: Validate pre-specified cut-offs in consecutive local patients.

items.title: Patients unable to complete exercise testing are dropped
items.whyItMatters: Excluding them overstates specificity and removes the frailest (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Classify inability to complete testing as low functional capacity by a pre-specified rule, with a sensitivity analysis.

items.title: Two grey sources cannot be appraised
items.whyItMatters: The gait speed cut-off and the combination rule come from undated, unrated reports (claim c5).
items.opportunity: Treat their figures as candidate values only, not as evidence.

items.title: Frail and older patients may be misclassified
items.whyItMatters: Joint pain and frailty affect both tests.
items.opportunity: Report accuracy for patients aged 75 and over and by frailty.

errorsFound: The two undated grey records have no year and no appraisable methods; they stay unrated rather than receiving guessed scores.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a validation study of pre-specified bedside test cut-offs in consecutive patients with blinded testing and a rule for patients who cannot complete the reference test.
summary: Four gaps; unvalidated cut-offs and dropped untestable patients are high severity.
